correctness.rationale: Direct substitution gives the two-by-two recurrence. Its trace, determinant, and discriminant were independently recomputed. For fixed product, the complex-root modulus decreases with the step sum and the dominant real root increases with it, so the minimum is at the real/complex transition when feasible and otherwise at the arithmetic-geometric boundary. The global product minimization follows from an exact derivative-sign identity. The adaptive product invariant follows algebraically from every published update branch. The packaged checker verifies the key identities and representative values.

value.rationale: Residual balancing changes only the primal/dual ratio while preserving their product. The scalar theorem gives a complete natural benchmark for that design choice: it locates the globally optimal product, exposes a symmetry-breaking critical-damping regime below \(p=1/2\), and distinguishes what ratio-only adaptation can tune from what it cannot. This is useful for evaluating product-adaptive extensions and spectral tuning rules, rather than an arbitrary scalar exercise.
